title: Variable Properties: Naming, Types, Labels, and Values

content.quick: Variable View in SPSS defines how the software interprets your questionnaire responses. Variable names cannot start with numbers or contain spaces; labels provide full survey text; value labels map numeric codes to categories; and measurement scales govern which statistical tests SPSS allows you to run.

blocks.explain: Setting up your variable properties in SPSS properly prevents syntax errors and ensures your output tables display clear, human-readable labels.

sentences.text: Correctly configuring variable properties in SPSS prevents catastrophic syntax errors and miscalculated statistical tests.
sentences.simple: Setting up your variable settings in SPSS properly stops mistakes before you run any calculations.
sentences.plain: Correctly configuring variable properties in SPSS prevents catastrophic syntax errors and miscalculated statistical tests.
sentences.technical: Proper variable parameterization within the SPSS data dictionary establishes mathematical constraints essential for parametric test validity.

sentences.text: Variable names in SPSS cannot exceed 64 bytes, cannot contain spaces, and cannot end with a period or start with a number.
sentences.simple: Variable names must be short, have no spaces, and must start with a letter (e.g. use TL_1 instead of 1_TL).
sentences.plain: Variable names in SPSS cannot exceed 64 bytes, cannot contain spaces, and cannot end with a period or start with a number.
sentences.technical: Identifier tokens in SPSS are subject to lexicographic constraints: strict 64-byte ceilings, initial alphabetical character requirements, and exclusion of reserved delimiters.

blocks.explain: The Measure column governs the mathematical permissions SPSS grants to a variable, distinguishing between Nominal, Ordinal, and Scale metrics.

sentences.text: The Measure column tells SPSS whether a variable represents categorical grouping data or continuous numerical quantities.
sentences.simple: The Measure column tells SPSS if a column is categories (like Gender) or continuous numbers (like Age or test scores).
sentences.plain: The Measure column tells SPSS whether a variable represents categorical grouping data or continuous numerical quantities.
sentences.technical: The scale taxonomy dictates whether mathematical operations like mean calculation or standard deviation estimation are mathematically legitimate.

visual.title: The 3 SPSS Measurement Levels
visual.caption: Always set 5-point and 7-point Likert composite variables to 'Scale' in SPSS.

sentences.text: Setting a continuous variable to 'Nominal' prevents SPSS from calculating means, standard deviations, and regression models in certain automated dialogs.
sentences.simple: If you leave your numbers set as 'Nominal', SPSS will treat them like category tags and refuse to run certain statistics.
sentences.plain: Setting a continuous variable to 'Nominal' prevents SPSS from calculating means, standard deviations, and regression models in certain automated dialogs.
sentences.technical: Misclassifying metric variables as nominal induces procedure lock-out across advanced SPSS charting and linear modeling procedures.

sentences.text: According to Field (2018), composite scale scores computed by averaging 5-point or 7-point Likert items are treated as continuous Scale data.
sentences.simple: When you average several Likert questions together, famous statisticians confirm you can treat that score as continuous Scale data.
sentences.plain: According to Field (2018), composite scale scores computed by averaging 5-point or 7-point Likert items are treated as continuous Scale data.
sentences.technical: Following psychometric consensus (Field, 2018; Tabachnick & Fidell, 2019), multi-item Likert composites satisfy quasi-interval properties, justifying parametric procedures.

blocks.explain: Value Labels map numerical codes to descriptive category titles, enabling lightning-fast numeric data entry while preserving readable output.

sentences.text: Value labels map internal numeric storage values to human-readable categories, eliminating the need to type text strings during data entry.
sentences.simple: Value labels let you type '1' or '2' on your keyboard instead of typing 'Male' or 'Female' hundreds of times.
sentences.plain: Value labels map internal numeric storage values to human-readable categories, eliminating the need to type text strings during data entry.
sentences.technical: Value labeling establishes an internal categorical lookup table, optimizing disk I/O and precluding alphanumeric data entry corruption.

sentences.text: Entering numbers rather than text strings accelerates data collection tenfold and completely eliminates spelling typos that fragment category counts.
sentences.simple: Typing numbers stops typos like 'Femlae' or 'male' with lowercase letters from creating separate accidental categories.
sentences.plain: Entering numbers rather than text strings accelerates data collection tenfold and completely eliminates spelling typos that fragment category counts.
sentences.technical: Numerical encoding guarantees homomorphic grouping, eliminating lexical fragmentation induced by capitalization or orthographic variance.

sentences.text: Configuring the Missing column with discrete missing values (such as -99 or 999) ensures uncompleted responses do not distort empirical means.
sentences.simple: Tell SPSS what number means 'no answer' (like -99) so it does not count empty answers into your averages.
sentences.plain: Configuring the Missing column with discrete missing values (such as -99 or 999) ensures uncompleted responses do not distort empirical means.
sentences.technical: Discrete missing value declaration isolates non-response tokens from mathematical vectors, preventing systemic bias in central tendency estimations.

questions.q: What happens if a researcher enters '99' for missing survey answers without declaring 99 in the Missing column?
options: SPSS will treat 99 as a real number, causing the variable mean to falsely inflate to an absurd value like 25.4
SPSS automatically recognizes that 99 means missing and deletes it
SPSS shuts down with an error message
questions.explanation: SPSS treats any undeclared number as genuine data. A single 99 in a 1-5 scale will completely corrupt your mean and standard deviation.

blocks.explain: Conduct a pre-analysis data screening audit using Frequencies to catch data entry typos before running formal hypothesis tests.

sentences.text: Before running correlation or regression models, researchers must audit their raw data for impossible entry codes using Frequency tables.
sentences.simple: Before running your main tests, run a quick Frequency check to see if anyone accidentally typed a '6' or '7' on a 1-5 scale.
sentences.plain: Before running correlation or regression models, researchers must audit their raw data for impossible entry codes using Frequency tables.
sentences.technical: Pre-analytical verification requires univariate frequency auditing across all survey variables to detect out-of-range typographical entries and boundary violations.

visual.title: Data Screening Audit Protocol

dos: Run Analyze -> Descriptive Statistics -> Frequencies on all survey items
Inspect Minimum and Maximum values: on a 1-5 scale, Minimum must be 1 and Maximum must be 5
Use Data -> Sort Cases to quickly find and fix out-of-range entry rows
donts: Never jump directly to regression without screening raw frequencies first
Do not ignore unexpected negative values in your minimum column
Never delete a respondent's entire row if only one item is missing

visual.caption: Five minutes of frequency screening prevents humiliating supervisor corrections.

sentences.text: If a frequency table shows a minimum of 0 or a maximum of 55 on a 5-point scale, a typographical entry mistake has occurred that must be rectified.
sentences.simple: If you see a 55 in your maximum column, someone accidentally hit the '5' key twice during data entry.
sentences.plain: If a frequency table shows a minimum of 0 or a maximum of 55 on a 5-point scale, a typographical entry mistake has occurred that must be rectified.
sentences.technical: Erroneous out-of-bound observations (e.g., x = 55 in a domain [1, 5]) induce severe leptokurtic skewness and distort covariance matrices.

questions.q: What is the quickest way in SPSS to locate the exact participant row containing a typographical data entry error like '55'?
options: Right-click the variable column in Data View and select 'Sort Descending' so the 55 appears at the top row
Re-type all 400 survey responses from scratch
Delete the entire SPSS software program and reinstall it
Print the entire dataset on 100 pages of paper and search with a magnifying glass
questions.explanation: Sorting the column descending puts the largest number (55) right on Row 1, allowing you to cross-reference the paper questionnaire and correct the typo in 5 seconds.

mistakes: Using spaces or leading numerals in variable names (e.g. '1 Q1' or 'Job Satisfaction').
Leaving questionnaire items as String variables instead of Numeric with Value Labels.
Leaving composite Likert scores set as Nominal instead of Scale.
Entering missing data codes like 99 without declaring them in the Missing column.
takeaways: Variable names are short syntax codes; Variable Labels hold full survey questions.
Always set multi-item composite constructs to Measure = Scale.
Use Value Labels to map 1=SD to 5=SA so data entry is fast, numeric, and error-free.
Run Frequencies on all variables to screen for out-of-range entry typos before running statistics.
